findings.title: Global mutable semaphore without thread-safe initialization

evidence.snippet:
_LLM_SEMAPHORE: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None
_LLM_CONCURRENCY: int = 3

findings.impact: Multiple asyncio tasks calling set_concurrency() or _get_semaphore() concurrently can trigger race conditions. The pattern `if _LLM_SEMAPHORE is None: _LLM_SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(...)` in _get_semaphore() is not atomic. Two tasks checking the None condition simultaneously could both create a new Semaphore, leading to inconsistent concurrency limiting and broken synchronization.
findings.recommendation: Use asyncio.Lock to protect the semaphore initialization. Alternatively, initialize the semaphore once at module load or use a thread-safe singleton pattern with double-checked locking and a lock.
findings.patch_hint: Add `_SEMAPHORE_LOCK = asyncio.Lock()` at module level. In _get_semaphore(), wrap the check-and-create in `async with _SEMAPHORE_LOCK:` to ensure only one task initializes the semaphore.
findings.test_hint: Write a test that spawns multiple concurrent tasks calling set_concurrency() followed by _get_semaphore() and verify only one Semaphore instance is created.

findings.title: Race condition in set_concurrency with global state reset

evidence.snippet:
def set_concurrency(n: int) -> None:
    global _LLM_SEMAPHORE, _LLM_CONCURRENCY
    _LLM_CONCURRENCY = max(1, n)
    _LLM_SEMAPHORE = None

findings.impact: Setting _LLM_SEMAPHORE to None while other tasks may be acquiring it in _get_semaphore() creates a race condition. If one task is in the middle of checking `if _LLM_SEMAPHORE is None:` while another calls set_concurrency(), the semaphore can be reset mid-flight, causing tasks to bypass concurrency limits or deadlock.
findings.recommendation: Protect set_concurrency() and _get_semaphore() with the same asyncio.Lock. Ensure semaphore updates are atomic and no task can observe partial state.
findings.patch_hint: Use `async with _SEMAPHORE_LOCK:` in both set_concurrency() (make it async) and _get_semaphore(). Alternatively, disallow runtime changes to concurrency or recreate the semaphore atomically.
findings.test_hint: Test concurrent calls to set_concurrency() and _get_semaphore() from multiple tasks and verify no semaphore is lost or duplicated.

all_findings.title: Global mutable semaphore without thread-safe initialization

evidence.snippet:
_LLM_SEMAPHORE: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None
_LLM_CONCURRENCY: int = 3

all_findings.impact: Multiple asyncio tasks calling set_concurrency() or _get_semaphore() concurrently can trigger race conditions. The pattern `if _LLM_SEMAPHORE is None: _LLM_SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(...)` in _get_semaphore() is not atomic. Two tasks checking the None condition simultaneously could both create a new Semaphore, leading to inconsistent concurrency limiting and broken synchronization.
all_findings.recommendation: Use asyncio.Lock to protect the semaphore initialization. Alternatively, initialize the semaphore once at module load or use a thread-safe singleton pattern with double-checked locking and a lock.
all_findings.patch_hint: Add `_SEMAPHORE_LOCK = asyncio.Lock()` at module level. In _get_semaphore(), wrap the check-and-create in `async with _SEMAPHORE_LOCK:` to ensure only one task initializes the semaphore.
all_findings.test_hint: Write a test that spawns multiple concurrent tasks calling set_concurrency() followed by _get_semaphore() and verify only one Semaphore instance is created.

all_findings.title: Race condition in set_concurrency with global state reset

evidence.snippet:
def set_concurrency(n: int) -> None:
    global _LLM_SEMAPHORE, _LLM_CONCURRENCY
    _LLM_CONCURRENCY = max(1, n)
    _LLM_SEMAPHORE = None

all_findings.impact: Setting _LLM_SEMAPHORE to None while other tasks may be acquiring it in _get_semaphore() creates a race condition. If one task is in the middle of checking `if _LLM_SEMAPHORE is None:` while another calls set_concurrency(), the semaphore can be reset mid-flight, causing tasks to bypass concurrency limits or deadlock.
all_findings.recommendation: Protect set_concurrency() and _get_semaphore() with the same asyncio.Lock. Ensure semaphore updates are atomic and no task can observe partial state.
all_findings.patch_hint: Use `async with _SEMAPHORE_LOCK:` in both set_concurrency() (make it async) and _get_semaphore(). Alternatively, disallow runtime changes to concurrency or recreate the semaphore atomically.
all_findings.test_hint: Test concurrent calls to set_concurrency() and _get_semaphore() from multiple tasks and verify no semaphore is lost or duplicated.

all_findings.title: Potential blocking I/O in async context with Path.read_text

evidence.snippet: raw = env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").strip()

all_findings.impact: Path.read_text() is synchronous blocking I/O. If called inside an async function (e.g. wrapped in an async CLI handler), it blocks the event loop, degrading concurrency and responsiveness. This pattern appears in a synchronous _load_env() context here, but if this code is invoked from an async entry point, it will block.
all_findings.recommendation: If the CLI runs in an async context (e.g. typer with async commands), use aiofiles or asyncio.to_thread() to offload file reads. If CLI is purely synchronous, this is acceptable but document that async code should not call _load_env().

all_findings.title: Fire-and-forget concurrent agent execution with asyncio.gather

evidence.snippet: reports: list[AgentReport] = await asyncio.gather(*[_run_agent(a) for a in agents])

all_findings.impact: asyncio.gather() without return_exceptions=True will propagate the first exception and cancel remaining tasks. If one agent crashes, others may not complete. The code has a try/except in _run_agent() which mitigates this, but if an exception escapes (e.g. from asyncio.gather itself), remaining agents are silently cancelled.
all_findings.recommendation: Add `return_exceptions=True` to asyncio.gather() to ensure all agents complete even if some fail. Then handle exceptions in the results list.
all_findings.patch_hint: Change to `await asyncio.gather(*[_run_agent(a) for a in agents], return_exceptions=True)` and filter/log exceptions in results.
